═══ IMPLEMENTED, RED→GREEN — and I deviated from one of my own acceptance criteria; reasoning below
so the verifier and a reader judge it rather than discover it. ═══

**THE FIX.** The qualified/unqualified decision moves out of two independent colon scans into ONE
helper, `config.split_provider_qualifier`:

    _PROVIDER_QUALIFIER_RE = re.compile(r"^[a-z][a-z0-9_-]*$")

    def split_provider_qualifier(model): 
        prefix, sep, rest = model.partition(":")
        if sep and rest and _PROVIDER_QUALIFIER_RE.match(prefix): return prefix, rest
        return None, model

Both former deciders now call it:
* `model_classes._resolve_target` — was `if ":" in model: return model` (which discarded the
  configured provider);
* `config.infer_provider` — was `model.split(":", 1)[0]` (which returned a fragment of the model id).

They were two separate wrong implementations of the same question, which is why they failed in the
same way; there is now one implementation and a test asserting they agree.

**RED FIRST, CONFIRMED.** `tests/unit/test_provider_qualifier.py`: pre-fix **6 failed, 15 passed**.
The 15 passing are the controls — already-qualified strings not double-prefixed, the unversioned
alias that always worked, and name-based inference — so the 6 failures could not be "nothing
resolves". Post-fix 21/21. One failure message is worth keeping as the record of the bug's shape:
`infer_provider returned 'anthropic.claude-opus-4-5-20251101-v1'`.

**DEVIATION FROM AN AC, STATED PLAINLY.** The criterion says the decision should be made "against the
REGISTERED PROVIDER SET rather than by the presence of a colon". I did the second half but not the
first: the test is the prefix's SHAPE (an identifier: lowercase, digits, `_`, `-`, and crucially NO
DOTS), not membership in a provider registry. Reasons, in order of weight:
 1. **The registry is not reachable here.** `_resolve_target` runs during CONFIG RESOLUTION.
    The live set is `ProviderSession._builders` — an INSTANCE attribute needing an `LLMConfig` — plus
    `_pydantic_ai_known_providers()`, which imports `pydantic_ai`. That is the OPTIONAL `[agents]`
    extra, and `rebar.llm` is deliberately stdlib-only at import. Consulting it would make config
    parsing depend on an optional package.
 2. **A hand-maintained whitelist would defeat the AC's own stated purpose** — "so a future provider
    name needs no second edit here". A whitelist needs an edit per provider; the shape test needs
    none, and already accepts names this repo does not register (`openai-chat`, `openai-responses`,
    `google_genai`), which are covered by tests.
 3. **The discriminator is factually dots.** Provider names in this stack are identifiers; Bedrock
    model ids are dotted (`us.anthropic.…`, `anthropic.…`). That is what the versioned-vs-alias
    evidence showed, and it is checked against both shapes.
If the operator prefers the registry reading, the honest cost is either an optional-import dependency
in config parsing or a whitelist that needs maintaining — I judged the shape test strictly better and
am flagging it rather than quietly re-interpreting the criterion.

**NOT DONE, and it is NOT in this ticket's description ACs** — the config-time fail-fast I proposed in
the earlier design comment (raise `LLMConfigError` at config read for a class whose provider/model
cannot be composed). With the qualifier fixed, the reported failure can no longer arise from a colon,
so this is now about a DIFFERENT input (a genuine typo like `provider = "bedrok"`), which still
surfaces late as an "outage". Worth its own ticket rather than widening this one; the gate's
fail-closed behaviour is untouched either way.

**REGRESSION SURFACE.** `infer_provider` has wide fan-in, so it was the risk. 656 passed across the
provider/model-class/runner/workflow areas (`test_model_class_ladder`, `test_model_classes`,
`test_bedrock_provider`, `test_llm_provider_factory`, `test_openai_compatible_provider`,
`test_pydantic_ai_runner`, `test_code_review_verifier_class`, all of `tests/unit/workflow/`).
`make typecheck` clean (407 files), `make lint` clean. Full unit suite running.

**Still-unqualified colon splits left alone deliberately:** `runner.py:328` and `providers.py:215`
split an ALREADY-QUALIFIED `resolved` string, where splitting on the first colon is correct and the
fix does not change their inputs; `evals/eval.py:101-102` is eval-only. Naming them so a reader does
not have to re-derive that they were considered.
